# Using the wiki

Choose the mode from the user's request and load only its references. Treat
`` as that request when the host has not substituted it.

- **Find pages or passages:** read [search](references/search.md). This is the
  complete ordinary lookup startup path; no maintenance preamble is needed.
- **Answer with citations:** read [query](references/query.md),
  [search](references/search.md), and the shared
  [evidence policy](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md).
- **Write original wiki documentation or validate what this authoring task wrote:**
  read [authoring](references/authoring.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), and
  [operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md).
- **Perform a requested native app action:** read
  [Obsidian commands](../wiki-maintainer/references/obsidian-cli.md) and
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Ordinary Markdown edits use
  exact-path filesystem access; an unavailable app does not block them.

Retrieval and unfiled answers are read-only: no operations, logs, commits or index
refreshes. Answering does not authorize filing an answer. Before any authorized
vault mutation, read [operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md)
and finish its scoped validation, commit, sync and remote verification unless the
user holds publication. Preserve foreign edits and immutable raw evidence.

For an answer that needs source discovery or captured-source ingestion, route to
[wiki-researcher](../wiki-researcher/SKILL.md) in the requested mode; a search miss
alone does not authorize either operation.

62	## Canonical placement for original project documentation
63	
64	- **`wiki/authored/`** is where original, primary content lives — advisory
65	  documentation, policy, house style, or any other work you're writing directly
66	  into the vault rather than deriving from a captured source. It is not a
67	  special case of the pipeline: it declares `sources: []` (the vault's existing
68	  disclosure for "rests on no external artifact," extended here as the default
69	  for the whole category) and is otherwise a wiki page like any other — living,
70	  revisable, never needing a `raw/` counterpart.
71	
72	  **When this page belongs to a multi-doc project**, it lives at
73	  `wiki/authored/<project>/[<subproject>/]<file>.md` — a real folder, not just a
74	  frontmatter tag, so related documents stay together. Every doc-kind has one canonical location, so the same request always
75	  resolves the same way, for every project, without re-deriving convention from
76	  whatever a prior session happened to name things:
77	
78	  | You hear | It lives at |
79	  |---|---|
80	  | "update the product documentation" / "the overview" | `<project>/overview.md` |
81	  | "document the architecture" | `<project>/architecture.md` |
82	  | "add/update the roadmap" | `<project>/roadmap.md` — **mostly generated**, see below |
83	  | "write a user guide" | `<project>/guides/user.md` |
84	  | "write a developer guide" | `<project>/guides/developer.md` |
85	  | "write an administrator guide" | `<project>/guides/administrator.md` |
86	  | "get me a diagram [for X]" | `<project>/diagrams/<x-slug>.md` |
87	  | "write up a reference doc on X" | `<project>/reference/<x-slug>.md` |
88	  | "record a decision about X" (ADR) | `<project>/decisions/<x-slug>-adr.md` |
89	  | "make a note about X" | `<project>/notes/<x-slug>.md` |
90	  | "add an item to the backlog" | `<project>/backlog/<item-slug>.md` — see below |
91	
92	  Set `project:` (a slug, one `/` deep at most for a sub-project, e.g.
93	  `acme-suite/migrator`) and `kind:` — one of `overview | architecture |
94	  reference | guide | diagram | decision | roadmap | note | backlog-item` —
95	  matching the folder you placed it in; both are optional and can be omitted
96	  for a genuinely standalone, project-less note. Use `_templates/authored-note.md`
97	  to start a page (`_templates/authored-decision.md` for an ADR,
98	  `_templates/authored-backlog-item.md` for a backlog item — see below).
99	  A project's `overview.md` may carry `repo:` (a git remote URL, `owner/name`, or a
100	  repository folder name; a list is allowed). `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/session-brief.mjs"`, run in
101	  a repository, uses it to find the project that repository belongs to and print its
102	  state page; the repository itself needs no change, and holds no project name.
103	  `kind: decision` additionally carries `decision-status: proposed | accepted |
104	  superseded | deprecated` (Nygard's ADR vocabulary) — keep it in sync with
105	  whatever the page's own `## Status` section says in prose. **Existing files
106	  are not renamed to fit this table** — only new ones follow it going forward;
107	  a bare canonical leaf name (`overview.md`) repeated across every project would
108	  be a guaranteed cross-project wikilink collision (see the identity rules below), so existing filenames stay as they are, just moved into
109	  their project's folder.
110	
111	  Because `overview.md` / `architecture.md` / `roadmap.md` are deliberately
112	  reused bare names across projects (each project gets its own), a bare
113	  `[[roadmap]]` link is ambiguous the moment a **second** project acquires one —
114	  it resolves to whichever one Obsidian's name index happens to pick, silently,
115	  with no error. **Any reference to one of these files from *outside* its own
116	  project must use the piped form naming the full path** —
117	  `[[wiki/authored/<project>/roadmap.md|<project> roadmap]]` — the same
118	  convention this vault already uses for other ambiguous bare titles (e.g.
119	  citing two source pages with the same title). A link from *within* the same
120	  project's own pages can stay bare.
121	
122	  Two rules decide a bare name before it counts as ambiguous. A file whose own name equals the link outranks files that only share that name as a `title:` or alias (a site that serves a case's syllabus and opinion under one title gives two clippings one title; the clipping named for the link is the one Obsidian opens). And in navigation a project's generated hub MOC (`moc/<project>.md`) yields to a page of the same name, so a bare `[[<project>]]` reaches the entity page; the MOC is still reached by `[[moc/<project>]]`. Two files with the same name stay ambiguous. After a refresh scoped to one project, the result's `staleCatalogs` names other projects' generated catalogs whose bare link your new pages made ambiguous; refresh each named project.
123	
124	  **The backlog is a folder of small items, never one growing document.** A
125	  tracked item is its own file, `<project>/backlog/<item-slug>.md`
126	  (`kind: backlog-item`, `backlog-status: planned | in-progress | shipped |
127	  blocked | dropped`). "Add an item" = create exactly one new small file.
128	  "Update an item" = edit exactly that one file's `backlog-status:` and body —
129	  **never append a new dated "Update (date): ..." paragraph on top of the old
130	  ones; edit the item's own text in place.** `git log`/`git blame` is the
131	  changelog now, not a stack of callouts inside the body. `<project>/roadmap.md`
132	  itself becomes a thin, mostly-generated index over `backlog/*.md` (run
133	  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backlog-gen.mjs" --apply` after adding/updating an item) —
134	  the same fenced-region contract `index.md` already uses: hand-written framing
135	  prose stays outside the fence, the itemized, always-current list lives inside
136	  it. Revise each item's current state in place so the roadmap stays a useful
137	  index rather than accumulating dated updates.
138	
139	  **A backlog item can say what it waits on.** List its prerequisites under `depends-on` as quoted wikilinks to other backlog items of the same project, for example `depends-on: ["[[other-item]]"]` (one scalar or a block sequence also works). A prerequisite is met once its item is shipped or dropped. The relation never changes the item's own status: a `blocked` item you set by hand stays under Blocked. The generated roadmap notes "waiting on" after each open item that has an unmet prerequisite, and lists every planned item whose declared prerequisites are all met under a trailing "Ready to start" section. An item that declares nothing is startable and is not listed there. A prerequisite in another project is rejected; keep the relation inside one project and link across projects in the item's text.
140	
141	  **List the backlog by lifecycle, not by page status.** Every backlog file has two fields that look alike: the page `status` (`draft` or `maintained`) and the lifecycle `backlog-status`, so a search for `status:` lists no planned items. `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backlog-list.mjs" [--project <name>] [--backlog-status planned,in-progress] [--startable] [--json]` is read-only, does not build the whole-vault graph, and prints one tab-separated line per item: project, lifecycle status, path, title, and `waiting on <items>` when a prerequisite is unmet. `--backlog-status` takes the five words above and `unrecognized` (the items a generated roadmap lists under "Unrecognized status"); `--startable` keeps planned items with no unmet prerequisite, whether or not they declare any. Exit 2 is bad input.
142	
143	  **A mature project can shorten its generated roadmap.** Two settings in the roadmap's own frontmatter, both off until you add them, so nothing changes by default: `backlog-titles: true` shows each item's first heading as its link text, and `backlog-shipped: collapse` replaces the Shipped list with a count and a link to a generated sibling page, `roadmap-shipped.md` (kind `reference`, created on first use, with its own fenced list). Run `backlog-gen.mjs --apply` or `refresh-catalogs.mjs` after changing a setting. A pipe or bracket in a heading is replaced by a space in the link text. Removing the collapse setting lists Shipped on the roadmap again but leaves `roadmap-shipped.md` for you to delete.
144	
145	  **A friction item says what produced its observation.** When an item states a behavior as tested or observed, paste the exact call arguments (or the script name) and the exact log or error text beside the claim, and mark a fact whose reading of the source disagrees with the run as unsettled until a run decides. Without them the claim cannot be reconciled with the source later without a rerun.
146	
147	  When `backlog-gen.mjs` (or `refresh-catalogs.mjs`) creates a roadmap that does not exist, the page starts with `type: authored`, `created`, `updated`, `status: draft`, `sources: []`, `ai-generated: true`, `project` and `kind: roadmap`. `reviewed` is omitted on purpose: nobody has reviewed a page a script just wrote. `created` and `updated` are the UTC day of the run and cannot be set from the command line. A dry run creates no page and no temp file. An existing roadmap is never rewritten outside the generated fence.
148	
149	  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"`'s `monolith candidates` line (a `wiki/authored/`
150	  page over ~3,000 words with several stacked dated-update callouts) is a
151	  secondary safety net for anything that still grows despite the format above —
152	  report it, don't silently keep appending.
153	
154	## Keeping project documentation honest
155	
156	The table above settles *where* a document goes. These settle whether it is still
157	worth reading a month later — each one is a failure that actually happens, not a
158	style preference.
159	
160	- **`architecture.md` is as-built, not as-planned.** The moment it describes
161	  something that does not exist, a reader cannot tell which half is true. Anything
162	  intended rather than shipped belongs in `roadmap.md` or a backlog item.
163	- **`roadmap.md` records state, not history.** It is the page most likely to be
164	  silently stale, and the failure is specific: it keeps listing as "next" three
165	  things that shipped a fortnight ago. **Update it in the same operation as the
166	  work** — a roadmap updated later is a roadmap updated never.
167	- **An ADR states context, decision, consequences — good AND bad — and status.**
168	  *A consequences section that lists only benefits is a sales pitch, not a record.*
169	  The reason to revisit a decision is always in the half that gets left out, so an
170	  ADR without costs has thrown away the only part that will matter.
171	- **Label a retrospective ADR as reconstructed.** Most projects start by writing up
172	  decisions already taken; that is legitimate and lossy. Reasoning recovered from
173	  code and commit history is not the reasoning that was used, and saying so is the
174	  difference between a record and a plausible story.
175	- **Record the failures.** Stalls, refuted hypotheses, and measurements that
176	  contradicted a confident diagnosis are the highest-value content in a project
177	  set, because they are precisely what nobody remembers and everybody repeats. If a
178	  fix was wrong twice before it was right, all three attempts belong on the page.
179	- **Distinguish "not built" from "built and broken".** From outside they look
180	  identical and only one of them is a bug. A reader who cannot tell will either
181	  re-implement something that exists or file a bug against something that does not.
182	- **The wiki owns intent; the repo owns behaviour.** When they disagree, the code
183	  wins on what happens and the wiki wins on what was meant — and the disagreement
184	  itself is worth writing down, because it is usually where the next defect is.
185	
186	## Validating what a task wrote
187	
188	Before committing, check exactly the pages the task wrote:
189	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file <ledger>`,
190	with the vault set as in the access reference.
191	
192	**The ledger** is the file `op-commit.mjs --paths-file` takes: a non-empty JSON array
193	of vault-relative paths with `/` separators (no drive prefix, backslash, empty segment,
194	`.` or `..`), for example `["wiki/authored/demo/guides/user.md","wiki/authored/demo/roadmap.md"]`.
195	Record each page you wrote with `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token> <path>...` (the log and
196	catalog scripts record theirs when given `--since`), then
197	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" show --since <token> --out <ledger>`
198	writes this file and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong (a path that was already
199	dirty before `op-begin`, a path that is not dirty now, a changed path nobody recorded). Writing
200	it by hand with your file tool still works. Keep it under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. A path with no file at that exact spelling is reported as `missing-file`: a page that
201	does not exist, or one whose letter case or Unicode form differs from the file on disk,
202	because a case-insensitive disk would otherwise drop that page's link checks without a word.
203	
204	**The result.** The command writes nothing and reads the whole vault (ambiguity is
205	vault-wide), but reports only ledger pages; `health.mjs` stays the whole-vault check.
206	Exit 0 is clean, 1 means defects (fix and rerun), 2 means an unusable ledger, unknown
207	flag or missing vault. The text report is one `path:line rule message` line per defect,
208	sorted by path then line, then `validate-authored: N pages checked, M defects`, with
209	`, K skipped` appended only when K is above zero (checked plus skipped is the number of
210	distinct ledger paths). `--json` prints
211	`{"version":1,"checked":N,"skipped":K,"defects":[{"path","line","rule","message"}]}`
212	instead, which is exactly what `validateAuthored()` in `scripts/validate-authored.mjs` returns. An absent frontmatter key is reported at line 1; a blank key at its own line.
213	
214	**Public pages.** A page written for a plugin's public repository must not name other projects or machines. `--terms-file <path>` (the owner's private list, kept outside every repository; the file `scripts/scan-private-terms.mjs` reads) adds a `private-term` defect for each ledger page whose text matches a term or a built-in machine pattern (a home-directory path, a GPU model, an invisible character), at its line, naming the rule number and never the text. `--terms-projects a,b` limits the check to pages whose `project:` (first segment) is listed, so a private project's own pages may name themselves. Without `--terms-file` the output is unchanged.
215	
216	Under `wiki/authored/`:
217	
218	- `missing-key`: `type`, `created`, `updated`, `status`, `ai-generated` and a
219	  `sources` line (`[]` is valid) must be present and not blank, so an unfilled
220	  template fails. A page in a project folder also needs `project` and `kind`, a
221	  decision `decision-status`, a backlog item `backlog-status`. `reviewed` is optional.
222	  A page missing one of those two statuses is judged by its declared `kind`, not its folder.
223	- `bad-value`: `type` is `authored`, `ai-generated` is `true` or `false`, and `kind`
224	  and the two statuses use the vocabularies above (the message lists them). The page
225	  `status` is checked for presence only, so `status: wip` passes: check its value
226	  yourself against `stub`, `draft` and `maintained`.
227	- `kind-folder-mismatch`, `project-folder-mismatch`: `kind` agrees with the folder
228	  or file in the table above, `project` with the project folder (case ignored). The
229	  project is the folder path above the first kind folder (`guides`, `diagrams`,
230	  `reference`, `decisions`, `notes`, `backlog`) below the top folder, so
231	  `notes/<topic>/x.md` is a note and `project` must equal that folder path exactly.
232	  With no kind folder, `project` may be the top folder or the top folder plus one
233	  sub-project. `overview.md`, `architecture.md` and `roadmap.md` expect their own
234	  kind when they sit in a project folder. A page directly under `wiki/authored/` has
235	  no project or kind expectation. A wrong-kind page in `backlog/` gets only
236	  `kind-folder-mismatch`.
237	
238	- `dependency-dangling`, `dependency-cross-project`, `dependency-self`, `dependency-cycle`,
239	  `dependency-malformed`, `dependency-misplaced`: a `depends-on` entry must be a
240	  wikilink to an existing backlog item of the same project (a note in `backlog/` is
241	  not an item). The message names the entry; a cycle names the whole loop and is
242	  reported on each ledger page in it. `dependency-misplaced` is `depends-on` on a page
243	  that is not a backlog item, where it is ignored. Only the item's own project backlog
244	  folder is read, so these checks add no second whole-vault scan.
245	
246	On every wiki content page: `ambiguous-link`, `malformed-link` (a hard-wrapped link
247	is one), `unresolved-citation`, `malformed-frontmatter` (the page's metadata is not
248	read because of a stray carriage return or an unclosed fence), `missing-evidence`,
249	`cites-retired-page` (the cited page is marked `citation-status: retired`, so it is not support)
250	and `unresolved-link`, which is
251	stricter than health (it keeps such links as unscored forward links): a task must
252	not leave a dead link. Code spans and fences are not scanned. An absent file is
253	`missing-file`; raw, log, template, root catalog, non-Markdown and dot-prefixed paths
254	are skipped and counted.

   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op relink --title "<summary>" --since <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger>`.
   A close with no `--paths-file` is refused while another operation is open. Verify the commit and index-refresh notices, push with `wiki-sync.mjs`
   (or close and push in one command with `wiki-sync.mjs --op <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<summary>"`), and
   verify that the update reached the configured upstream. The authoring request
   includes this completion step unless the user explicitly holds publication;
   do not ask another routine permission question or leave the push to the user.
   If the sync is refused because uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes (exit 3), read "Refused sync" in the
   [operations reference](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md): never reset, check out, stash or delete a file you did not write.

**Done only when** the requested documentation and affected catalogs are
validated, its log and operation commit are recorded, and remote publication is
verified. Report explicit holds, local-only results and failed sync precisely;
do not call a local commit published.

## Canonical placement for original project documentation

- **`wiki/authored/`** is where original, primary content lives — advisory
  documentation, policy, house style, or any other work you're writing directly
  into the vault rather than deriving from a captured source. It is not a
  special case of the pipeline: it declares `sources: []` (the vault's existing
  disclosure for "rests on no external artifact," extended here as the default
  for the whole category) and is otherwise a wiki page like any other — living,
  revisable, never needing a `raw/` counterpart.

  **When this page belongs to a multi-doc project**, it lives at
  `wiki/authored/<project>/[<subproject>/]<file>.md` — a real folder, not just a
  frontmatter tag, so related documents stay together. Every doc-kind has one canonical location, so the same request always
  resolves the same way, for every project, without re-deriving convention from
  whatever a prior session happened to name things:

  | You hear | It lives at |
  |---|---|
  | "update the product documentation" / "the overview" | `<project>/overview.md` |
  | "document the architecture" | `<project>/architecture.md` |
  | "add/update the roadmap" | `<project>/roadmap.md` — **mostly generated**, see below |
  | "write a user guide" | `<project>/guides/user.md` |
  | "write a developer guide" | `<project>/guides/developer.md` |
  | "write an administrator guide" | `<project>/guides/administrator.md` |
  | "get me a diagram [for X]" | `<project>/diagrams/<x-slug>.md` |
  | "write up a reference doc on X" | `<project>/reference/<x-slug>.md` |
  | "record a decision about X" (ADR) | `<project>/decisions/<x-slug>-adr.md` |
  | "make a note about X" | `<project>/notes/<x-slug>.md` |
  | "add an item to the backlog" | `<project>/backlog/<item-slug>.md` — see below |

  Set `project:` (a slug, one `/` deep at most for a sub-project, e.g.
  `acme-suite/migrator`) and `kind:` — one of `overview | architecture |
  reference | guide | diagram | decision | roadmap | note | backlog-item` —
  matching the folder you placed it in; both are optional and can be omitted
  for a genuinely standalone, project-less note. Use `_templates/authored-note.md`
  to start a page (`_templates/authored-decision.md` for an ADR,
  `_templates/authored-backlog-item.md` for a backlog item — see below).
  A project's `overview.md` may carry `repo:` (a git remote URL, `owner/name`, or a
  repository folder name; a list is allowed). `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/session-brief.mjs"`, run in
  a repository, uses it to find the project that repository belongs to and print its
  state page; the repository itself needs no change, and holds no project name.
  `kind: decision` additionally carries `decision-status: proposed | accepted |
  superseded | deprecated` (Nygard's ADR vocabulary) — keep it in sync with
  whatever the page's own `## Status` section says in prose. **Existing files
  are not renamed to fit this table** — only new ones follow it going forward;
  a bare canonical leaf name (`overview.md`) repeated across every project would
  be a guaranteed cross-project wikilink collision (see the identity rules below), so existing filenames stay as they are, just moved into
  their project's folder.

  Because `overview.md` / `architecture.md` / `roadmap.md` are deliberately
  reused bare names across projects (each project gets its own), a bare
  `[[roadmap]]` link is ambiguous the moment a **second** project acquires one —
  it resolves to whichever one Obsidian's name index happens to pick, silently,
  with no error. **Any reference to one of these files from *outside* its own
  project must use the piped form naming the full path** —
  `[[wiki/authored/<project>/roadmap.md|<project> roadmap]]` — the same
  convention this vault already uses for other ambiguous bare titles (e.g.
  citing two source pages with the same title). A link from *within* the same
  project's own pages can stay bare.

  Two rules decide a bare name before it counts as ambiguous. A file whose own name equals the link outranks files that only share that name as a `title:` or alias (a site that serves a case's syllabus and opinion under one title gives two clippings one title; the clipping named for the link is the one Obsidian opens). And in navigation a project's generated hub MOC (`moc/<project>.md`) yields to a page of the same name, so a bare `[[<project>]]` reaches the entity page; the MOC is still reached by `[[moc/<project>]]`. Two files with the same name stay ambiguous. After a refresh scoped to one project, the result's `staleCatalogs` names other projects' generated catalogs whose bare link your new pages made ambiguous; refresh each named project.

  **The backlog is a folder of small items, never one growing document.** A
  tracked item is its own file, `<project>/backlog/<item-slug>.md`
  (`kind: backlog-item`, `backlog-status: planned | in-progress | shipped |
  blocked | dropped`). "Add an item" = create exactly one new small file.
  "Update an item" = edit exactly that one file's `backlog-status:` and body —
  **never append a new dated "Update (date): ..." paragraph on top of the old
  ones; edit the item's own text in place.** `git log`/`git blame` is the
  changelog now, not a stack of callouts inside the body. `<project>/roadmap.md`
  itself becomes a thin, mostly-generated index over `backlog/*.md` (run
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backlog-gen.mjs" --apply` after adding/updating an item) —
  the same fenced-region contract `index.md` already uses: hand-written framing
  prose stays outside the fence, the itemized, always-current list lives inside
  it. Revise each item's current state in place so the roadmap stays a useful
  index rather than accumulating dated updates.

  **A backlog item can say what it waits on.** List its prerequisites under `depends-on` as quoted wikilinks to other backlog items of the same project, for example `depends-on: ["[[other-item]]"]` (one scalar or a block sequence also works). A prerequisite is met once its item is shipped or dropped. The relation never changes the item's own status: a `blocked` item you set by hand stays under Blocked. The generated roadmap notes "waiting on" after each open item that has an unmet prerequisite, and lists every planned item whose declared prerequisites are all met under a trailing "Ready to start" section. An item that declares nothing is startable and is not listed there. A prerequisite in another project is rejected; keep the relation inside one project and link across projects in the item's text.

  **List the backlog by lifecycle, not by page status.** Every backlog file has two fields that look alike: the page `status` (`draft` or `maintained`) and the lifecycle `backlog-status`, so a search for `status:` lists no planned items. `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/backlog-list.mjs" [--project <name>] [--backlog-status planned,in-progress] [--startable] [--json]` is read-only, does not build the whole-vault graph, and prints one tab-separated line per item: project, lifecycle status, path, title, and `waiting on <items>` when a prerequisite is unmet. `--backlog-status` takes the five words above and `unrecognized` (the items a generated roadmap lists under "Unrecognized status"); `--startable` keeps planned items with no unmet prerequisite, whether or not they declare any. Exit 2 is bad input.

  **A mature project can shorten its generated roadmap.** Two settings in the roadmap's own frontmatter, both off until you add them, so nothing changes by default: `backlog-titles: true` shows each item's first heading as its link text, and `backlog-shipped: collapse` replaces the Shipped list with a count and a link to a generated sibling page, `roadmap-shipped.md` (kind `reference`, created on first use, with its own fenced list). Run `backlog-gen.mjs --apply` or `refresh-catalogs.mjs` after changing a setting. A pipe or bracket in a heading is replaced by a space in the link text. Removing the collapse setting lists Shipped on the roadmap again but leaves `roadmap-shipped.md` for you to delete.

  **A friction item says what produced its observation.** When an item states a behavior as tested or observed, paste the exact call arguments (or the script name) and the exact log or error text beside the claim, and mark a fact whose reading of the source disagrees with the run as unsettled until a run decides. Without them the claim cannot be reconciled with the source later without a rerun.

  When `backlog-gen.mjs` (or `refresh-catalogs.mjs`) creates a roadmap that does not exist, the page starts with `type: authored`, `created`, `updated`, `status: draft`, `sources: []`, `ai-generated: true`, `project` and `kind: roadmap`. `reviewed` is omitted on purpose: nobody has reviewed a page a script just wrote. `created` and `updated` are the UTC day of the run and cannot be set from the command line. A dry run creates no page and no temp file. An existing roadmap is never rewritten outside the generated fence.

  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"`'s `monolith candidates` line (a `wiki/authored/`
  page over ~3,000 words with several stacked dated-update callouts) is a
  secondary safety net for anything that still grows despite the format above —
  report it, don't silently keep appending.

## Keeping project documentation honest

The table above settles *where* a document goes. These settle whether it is still
worth reading a month later — each one is a failure that actually happens, not a
style preference.

- **`architecture.md` is as-built, not as-planned.** The moment it describes
  something that does not exist, a reader cannot tell which half is true. Anything
  intended rather than shipped belongs in `roadmap.md` or a backlog item.
- **`roadmap.md` records state, not history.** It is the page most likely to be
  silently stale, and the failure is specific: it keeps listing as "next" three
  things that shipped a fortnight ago. **Update it in the same operation as the
  work** — a roadmap updated later is a roadmap updated never.
- **An ADR states context, decision, consequences — good AND bad — and status.**
  *A consequences section that lists only benefits is a sales pitch, not a record.*
  The reason to revisit a decision is always in the half that gets left out, so an
  ADR without costs has thrown away the only part that will matter.
- **Label a retrospective ADR as reconstructed.** Most projects start by writing up
  decisions already taken; that is legitimate and lossy. Reasoning recovered from
  code and commit history is not the reasoning that was used, and saying so is the
  difference between a record and a plausible story.
- **Record the failures.** Stalls, refuted hypotheses, and measurements that
  contradicted a confident diagnosis are the highest-value content in a project
  set, because they are precisely what nobody remembers and everybody repeats. If a
  fix was wrong twice before it was right, all three attempts belong on the page.
- **Distinguish "not built" from "built and broken".** From outside they look
  identical and only one of them is a bug. A reader who cannot tell will either
  re-implement something that exists or file a bug against something that does not.
- **The wiki owns intent; the repo owns behaviour.** When they disagree, the code
  wins on what happens and the wiki wins on what was meant — and the disagreement
  itself is worth writing down, because it is usually where the next defect is.

## Validating what a task wrote

Before committing, check exactly the pages the task wrote:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file <ledger>`,
with the vault set as in the access reference.

**The ledger** is the file `op-commit.mjs --paths-file` takes: a non-empty JSON array
of vault-relative paths with `/` separators (no drive prefix, backslash, empty segment,
`.` or `..`), for example `["wiki/authored/demo/guides/user.md","wiki/authored/demo/roadmap.md"]`.
Record each page you wrote with `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token> <path>...` (the log and
catalog scripts record theirs when given `--since`), then
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" show --since <token> --out <ledger>`
writes this file and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong (a path that was already
dirty before `op-begin`, a path that is not dirty now, a changed path nobody recorded). Writing
it by hand with your file tool still works. Keep it under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. A path with no file at that exact spelling is reported as `missing-file`: a page that
does not exist, or one whose letter case or Unicode form differs from the file on disk,
because a case-insensitive disk would otherwise drop that page's link checks without a word.

**The result.** The command writes nothing and reads the whole vault (ambiguity is
vault-wide), but reports only ledger pages; `health.mjs` stays the whole-vault check.
Exit 0 is clean, 1 means defects (fix and rerun), 2 means an unusable ledger, unknown
flag or missing vault. The text report is one `path:line rule message` line per defect,
sorted by path then line, then `validate-authored: N pages checked, M defects`, with
`, K skipped` appended only when K is above zero (checked plus skipped is the number of
distinct ledger paths). `--json` prints
`{"version":1,"checked":N,"skipped":K,"defects":[{"path","line","rule","message"}]}`
instead, which is exactly what `validateAuthored()` in `scripts/validate-authored.mjs` returns. An absent frontmatter key is reported at line 1; a blank key at its own line.

**Public pages.** A page written for a plugin's public repository must not name other projects or machines. `--terms-file <path>` (the owner's private list, kept outside every repository; the file `scripts/scan-private-terms.mjs` reads) adds a `private-term` defect for each ledger page whose text matches a term or a built-in machine pattern (a home-directory path, a GPU model, an invisible character), at its line, naming the rule number and never the text. `--terms-projects a,b` limits the check to pages whose `project:` (first segment) is listed, so a private project's own pages may name themselves. Without `--terms-file` the output is unchanged.

Under `wiki/authored/`:

- `missing-key`: `type`, `created`, `updated`, `status`, `ai-generated` and a
  `sources` line (`[]` is valid) must be present and not blank, so an unfilled
  template fails. A page in a project folder also needs `project` and `kind`, a
  decision `decision-status`, a backlog item `backlog-status`. `reviewed` is optional.
  A page missing one of those two statuses is judged by its declared `kind`, not its folder.
- `bad-value`: `type` is `authored`, `ai-generated` is `true` or `false`, and `kind`
  and the two statuses use the vocabularies above (the message lists them). The page
  `status` is checked for presence only, so `status: wip` passes: check its value
  yourself against `stub`, `draft` and `maintained`.
- `kind-folder-mismatch`, `project-folder-mismatch`: `kind` agrees with the folder
  or file in the table above, `project` with the project folder (case ignored). The
  project is the folder path above the first kind folder (`guides`, `diagrams`,
  `reference`, `decisions`, `notes`, `backlog`) below the top folder, so
  `notes/<topic>/x.md` is a note and `project` must equal that folder path exactly.
  With no kind folder, `project` may be the top folder or the top folder plus one
  sub-project. `overview.md`, `architecture.md` and `roadmap.md` expect their own
  kind when they sit in a project folder. A page directly under `wiki/authored/` has
  no project or kind expectation. A wrong-kind page in `backlog/` gets only
  `kind-folder-mismatch`.

- `dependency-dangling`, `dependency-cross-project`, `dependency-self`, `dependency-cycle`,
  `dependency-malformed`, `dependency-misplaced`: a `depends-on` entry must be a
  wikilink to an existing backlog item of the same project (a note in `backlog/` is
  not an item). The message names the entry; a cycle names the whole loop and is
  reported on each ledger page in it. `dependency-misplaced` is `depends-on` on a page
  that is not a backlog item, where it is ignored. Only the item's own project backlog
  folder is read, so these checks add no second whole-vault scan.

On every wiki content page: `ambiguous-link`, `malformed-link` (a hard-wrapped link
is one), `unresolved-citation`, `malformed-frontmatter` (the page's metadata is not
read because of a stray carriage return or an unclosed fence), `missing-evidence`,
`cites-retired-page` (the cited page is marked `citation-status: retired`, so it is not support)
and `unresolved-link`, which is
stricter than health (it keeps such links as unscored forward links): a task must
not leave a dead link. Code spans and fences are not scanned. An absent file is
`missing-file`; raw, log, template, root catalog, non-Markdown and dot-prefixed paths
are skipped and counted.

2	
3	Use this contract for every ordinary vault write, including standalone clipping,
4	authoring and applying triage decisions. Read-only search, query, health, freshness
5	and preview work do not open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes.
6	
7	`index.md`'s generated catalog is derived: regenerate it with `index-gen.mjs`,
8	never hand-edit its fence or read-modify-write the file. Manual framing outside
9	the fence is preserved. A catalog already dirty from another writer remains
10	theirs: refresh safe project catalogs separately and report a deferred global
11	refresh rather than adopt foreign edits merely to close this operation.
12	
13	**Own the update through verified publication.** An authorized wiki edit includes
14	validation, the scoped operation commit, and pushing to its configured upstream
15	with `wiki-sync.mjs`, followed by remote verification. Finish those steps without
16	asking a separate routine permission question. An explicit user instruction to
17	hold publication or keep the work local overrides this default. A local commit
18	or a closed token alone does not publish the update. If a remote is absent or sync
19	fails, report the work as unpublished with its exact next action. Never create a
20	remote or repository merely to satisfy this rule. A token is not resolved merely
21	because its file was deleted; account for the work and verify the outcome.
22	
23	1. **Resolve scope and authorization.** Read the vault's instructions. Existing
24	   session authorization counts: a request to make a wiki update includes its
25	   normal commit-and-sync completion unless an explicit hold applies. A request to
26	   answer/search does not authorize filing a new page. Purge requires its specific
27	   reviewed plan and publication approval; do not replace those with this rule.
28	2. **Open before the first write.** Run `op-begin.mjs --op <op>` and save its token.
29	   On task resumption, reconcile a saved token before opening another one. Keep
30	   the operation type, title, owned-path ledger, log path and last completed phase
31	   with it so recovery can distinguish unfinished work from an already closed step.
32	   It snapshots already-dirty paths; `op-commit` excludes them. It does not isolate
33	   simultaneous edits to the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets; preserve
34	   pre-existing changes and report exclusions instead of sweeping them into a commit.
35	   With concurrent writers, maintain an explicit ledger of the exact vault-relative
36	   files this operation owns, including its log and generated catalogs when safe.
37	   Let the writers keep it: give `--since <token>` to every clipper, to `log-entry.mjs`,
38	   to `index-gen.mjs` and to `refresh-catalogs.mjs --apply`, each of which records the
39	   exact path it writes (unquoted UTF-8, so a name with an em dash survives), and record
40	   a page you wrote with your own file tools using `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token>
41	   <path>...`. `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <file>` writes the JSON array
42	   `--paths-file` takes and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong: recorded
43	   paths that were already dirty before `op-begin`, recorded paths that are not dirty
44	   now, and changed paths nobody recorded (another writer's, or one you forgot; it
45	   never claims them). Do not rebuild the set from `git show` or `git status`: git
46	   prints a non-ASCII name in quotes with octal escapes unless told otherwise, and a
47	   name lost that way is lost without an error.
48	   Pass a JSON array of those paths using `op-commit.mjs --paths-file <file>`;
49	   keep the manifest under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. This narrows the
50	   newly dirty delta and reports other new paths as outside scope. A ledger path that
51	   was already dirty when you ran `op-begin` is refused, not skipped: `op-commit` exits 1,
52	   names it and keeps the token. If this operation wrote it, run the same `op-commit`
53	   again with `--include <path>` for each (or `--include-from <file>`); if another writer
54	   owns it, take it out of the ledger. **Create new files only after `op-begin`**: a page
55	   written first counts as already dirty. It does not isolate simultaneous edits to the
56	   same file.

58	   dirty since `op-begin`, which cannot tell this operation's new files from another
59	   open operation's. So while any other operation token exists, of any age (age cannot
60	   show that an operation was abandoned), such a close is refused: `op-commit: this
61	   close has no --paths-file and another operation is open: <token> (<op>), ...`. It
62	   exits 1, commits nothing, keeps the token, and prints the way out: `op-ledger.mjs
63	   show --since <token> --out <ledger>`, then the same `op-commit` with `--paths-file

67	   line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl`; see "Refusal record" below.

87	   with date/op/title frontmatter and a grep-friendly heading. Use the existing
88	   operation vocabulary (ingest, discover, query, lint, relink); authoring uses
89	   relink. Never append to a shared aggregate log; browse through `log.base`. Pass
90	   `--since <token>`: the entry's name carries a timestamp known only now, and the
91	   ledger is how it reaches the close.
92	6. **Commit and inspect.** Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`,
93	   read what it lists as unclaimed, then `op-commit.mjs --op <op> --title "<title>"
94	   --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused
95	   while any other operation is open (the guard, step 2). Verify its result and the actual changed paths. Never `git add -A`.
96	   The helper attempts a semantic index refresh after committing; inspect notices
97	   for missing backends, skipped work or partial builds. A commit does not establish
98	   index freshness. Report a non-git vault as local-only; do not claim a commit.
99	7. **Push and verify your update.** `op-commit` itself never pushes. The plugin
100	   scripts own the vault's git, so sync with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"`,
101	   not a bare `git push`: it fetches, rebases onto the upstream (never a merge commit),
102	   pushes, retries once when another machine pushed first, and verifies against a fresh
103	   fetch. Run it after `op-commit`, never between edits; it names any operation still
104	   open. A conflict aborts the rebase, exits 1 and names the files; the local commits are
105	   intact. Report it and stop: do not force, resolve by guessing, or claim success.
106	   `rebase-failed` is different: the rebase never started (usually a held `.git/index.lock`),
107	   so no files are named and nothing changed. Wait for the other git process, never delete
108	   a lock, and run `wiki-sync` again. The line gives the lock's age; git records no holder,
109	   so a lock that stays old with no git process running is for the owner to judge.
110	   Older versions printed a held lock as a conflict in "unknown files": an empty file list
111	   means it was not a content conflict. Any sync, yours or another writer's, stashes and
112	   restores every uncommitted tracked file, so their modification times change and a CRLF
113	   file can come back LF with git's content unchanged; check line endings and content
114	   just before `op-commit`, not before an earlier sync.
115	   Inspect the sync result and verify the operation's resulting commit is included
116	   in the freshly fetched upstream. After a rebase, identify it by its unique log
117	   path and verify its actual changed paths rather than assuming its old SHA.
118	   Do not stop at a local commit, delegate publication to Obsidian Git, or ask the
119	   user to push work you are responsible for. Inspect outgoing commits first;
120	   coordinate rather than publish unrelated or explicitly held local commits.
121	   `--commit-local` first commits hand edits made outside any operation (the owner's
122	   own Obsidian edits) in one scoped `sync:` commit; it refuses while any operation is
123	   open, because dirty files cannot then be attributed. Use ordinary sync for your
124	   operation; do not use `--commit-local` to sweep another writer's unfinished work.
125	   When the user explicitly holds publication, retain the local commit and report
126	   that it is unpushed. Without an upstream, report local-only completion.
127	
128	   **Close and publish in one command.** `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>` closes that one
129	   operation through the same close `op-commit` makes, then runs the normal sync and
130	   verifies against a fresh fetch. The scope is `--paths-file <ledger>` when given;
131	   otherwise the paths the operation's writers recorded (`op-ledger.mjs`), when it has
132	   any; otherwise an unscoped close, which the guard refuses while another operation
133	   is open. `--title "<title>"` is the commit message (default `published with
134	   wiki-sync --op`; the subject is `<op>: <title>`). It never closes a token it was not
135	   given, and it cannot be combined with `--commit-local` (a usage error, exit 1).
136	   Success prints `closed operation <token>: committed <sha7> (<n> file(s))`, then the
137	   normal sync lines, exit 0. After a landed close it prints the same hard-wrapped
138	   wikilink warning `op-commit` does and refreshes the semantic index. A refused or
139	   failed close (token not open, unreadable `--paths-file`, the guard, a pre-dirty
140	   path, a git failure) prints a line starting `not committed:` to stderr, exits 1,
141	   pushes nothing and keeps the token. A close that landed whose sync then failed
142	   prints a line starting `committed, not published:` with the short sha, exits 1, and
143	   the token is gone because the commit exists; run `wiki-sync.mjs` again once the
144	   cause is fixed. Pass `--paths-file` instead of relying on the recorded paths when
145	   you have also written pages with tools that do not record them.
146	
147	   Without `--op`, `wiki-sync` also prints, for each open operation that has recorded
148	   paths still uncommitted, `operation <token> (<op>) has <n> recorded path(s) not
149	   committed; if it is yours, close and publish it with: node scripts/wiki-sync.mjs
150	   --op <token>`. It is a line, not a failure: a sync cannot know whose operation it
151	   is, so the exit code is unchanged and already-committed work is still pushed. It
152	   follows the once-per-set, once-a-day rule of the open-operations note, keyed by
153	   token and recorded count, so it is said again when an operation records more. An
154	   open operation with no recorded paths gets only the existing note.
155	
156	## Recovery and token ownership
157	
158	- **Retry the same operation.** After a recoverable failure, inspect the token,
159	  exact owned files and actual commits before retrying the failed step. Resolve
160	  an understood cause within the authorized scope without another confirmation.
161	  A failed Git close keeps its token; retry that `op-commit`, not the edits or an
162	  already-written log. Never delete a Git lock or guess at a content conflict.
163	- **Reconcile uncertain completion.** A timeout may have occurred after a commit
164	  or token removal. Verify the actual commit's subject and path membership, owned
165	  content and validation state. A completed no-op or already-committed operation
166	  with a retained token still closes through its own scoped `op-commit`; an empty
167	  delta alone does not prove completion. If the token is already gone, verify
168	  closure and continue from the next unfinished step rather than opening a new
169	  token or replaying work. After a sync rebase, locate the operation through its
170	  unique log path and recheck the resulting commit instead of relying on its old SHA.
171	- **Respect holds and ownership.** Do not close a user-held operation. A delegated
172	  worker reports its owned paths and validation to its enclosing operation's named
173	  owner rather than closing the parent's token. The hand-off is the ledger: the brief
174	  gives the worker the parent's token; the worker records each path it writes with
175	  `op-ledger.mjs add --since <parent token> <path>...` (a clipper it runs takes
176	  `--since` too) and reports its validation; it never runs `op-commit` or `op-abort`.
177	  The owner runs `op-ledger.mjs show --since <parent token>`, resolves whatever it
178	  lists as unclaimed, and closes once. That owner remains responsible for
179	  the scoped commit, push and remote verification; delegation does not drop the
180	  publication step. Leave other agents' tokens alone unless ownership was explicitly transferred;
181	  tokens contain an opening dirty-path snapshot, not proof of who owns later edits.
182	- **Leave actionable blockers.** If safe progress requires an unresolved conflict,
183	  missing authorization or another owner's action, retain the operation and record
184	  its token, owned paths, completed steps, pending work and exact next action. Report
185	  that blocker or ownership handoff; do not claim completion or silently abandon it.
186	
187	**Abandoned tokens.** List retained tokens with
188	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-cleanup.mjs"` (a dry run). Older than 24
189	hours means a review candidate, not proven abandonment; these tokens still block
190	`wiki-sync --commit-local`. For a verified-abandoned operation you own, with no
191	unfinished work or user hold, apply cleanup with its explicit `--apply --token <id>`
192	without another approval. Prefer normal `op-commit` closure when the saved operation
193	can be completed. `--hours <n>` changes the age filter, with a one-hour minimum;
194	respect that eligibility and verify removal. Never sweep tokens by age or delete
195	them manually. Token files are local Git-ignored state, not cross-machine locks.
196	The paths an operation's writers recorded sit in `<token>.paths.jsonl` beside the
197	token. `op-commit` (when the close lands), `op-abort` and a stale token removed by
198	`op-cleanup` take it with them; `op-cleanup` also lists a ledger whose token is
199	already gone and removes it only with `--apply --token <that id>`.
200	
201	**Stopping early.** A session that opened an operation and will not finish it, or whose work landed another way, drops its own token with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-abort.mjs" --since <token>`. It removes that one token whatever its age and nothing else: the files the operation wrote stay in the working tree, uncommitted, for a later operation to commit. Do not use it on a token another session holds. Open operations are visible without running a sync: `health` and `session-brief` print a line when any are open, and `wiki-sync` mentions other writers' operations once for a given set of tokens, again when the set changes, and once a day while it stays true.
202	
203	**Refused sync.** `wiki-sync` refuses to integrate while uncommitted edits overlap files
204	that the upstream changed: it prints `uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes in
205	<files>` and exits 3, the one exit code for this refusal (every other failure exits 1).
206	It changes nothing: no commit, stash or checkout, and the files and open tokens are
207	untouched. With no operation open the dirty files are hand edits, and the message is that
208	one line ending `commit them (or finish the operation) and sync again`. With an operation
209	open the message is longer: one line per overlapping file, `<file>: recorded by operation
210	<token> (<op>)` when an open operation's recorded ledger names the file and it is still
211	dirty, otherwise `<file>: not recorded by any open operation`; then `Open operations:
212	<token> (<op>), ...`; then `If you wrote these edits, finish your operation
213	(wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>) and sync again.` (the token is filled in only when exactly one
214	open operation recorded an overlapping file, otherwise the line shows the literal
215	`<token>`); then `If you did not, leave them exactly as they are:
216	do not reset, checkout, stash or delete them. Wait for their owner to close the operation, then sync again.` That
217	last instruction is the rule: a file you did not write is not yours to reset, check out,
218	stash or delete to get the sync through. Wait, and sync again after its owner closes. The
219	`recorded by` line is a hint, not proof of ownership. It reads only what writers recorded
220	with `--since` or `op-ledger.mjs add` (a generated file such as `index.md` is recorded only
221	when `index-gen` ran with `--since`) and ignores a ledger path that is not dirty now, an
222	unreadable ledger and the opening snapshot in a token, which says what was already dirty,
223	not who wrote it. `not recorded by any open operation` therefore does not mean no one is
224	writing the file. Each refusal also appends a counts-only line to the refusal record below.
225	
226	**Refusal record.** Each `op-commit` close that is refused and keeps its token, and each
227	`wiki-sync` that stops on an overlap (see "Refused sync"), appends
228	one JSON line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl` (local, Git-ignored): `at` (ISO
229	time), `op`, `kind` and `paths`. `paths` is a number and never a path name. `kind` is
230	`pre-dirty` (a ledger path already dirty before `op-begin` and not adopted; `paths` is
231	how many), `evidence` (a declared size or hash that does not match what git would store;
232	`paths` is the size of the evidence map), `unscoped` (the guard; `paths` is how many
233	delta paths the close would have committed) or `sync-overlap` (`op` is `wiki-sync`;
234	`paths` is how many files overlap). A close that lands appends nothing, and a
235	failed append (a directory in the file's place, a read-only disk) changes neither the
236	message nor the exit code. `health` prints `Recorded refusals: N (pre-dirty a,
237	evidence b, unscoped c, sync-overlap d).` only when N is above zero, and `health --json`
238	always carries `opRefusals` as `{ total, preDirty, evidence, unscoped, syncOverlap }`. The
239	line was `Recorded op-commit refusals: N (...)` in 0.85.0. Like the open-operations line it
240	sits outside the defect count. The file is never trimmed by the plugin and a line that is
241	not a record of a known kind counts as nothing.
242	
243	**Git ownership.** The plugin's scripts make the scoped commits and the sync: `op-commit`
244	commits what one operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. A new
245	vault's `vault-schema.md` (written by `wiki-init`) carries the same statement; an existing
246	vault keeps its own file. The Obsidian Git plugin stays installed for its source-control
247	view and for pulling. Its auto-commit and auto-push must be off (auto commit-and-sync
248	interval 0, commit on file change off, auto push interval 0): they commit half-finished
249	operation edits under "vault backup" and leave `op-commit` an empty delta. `wiki-sync`
250	warns when they are on. Every machine sharing the vault needs the same setting. An
251	instruction elsewhere that says Obsidian Git is the sync engine is stale.
252	
253	**Done only when** the requested change is validated, applicable catalogs and one
254	operation log are recorded, the operation commit is verified (or its precise
255	limitation reported), and its push and remote publication are verified. A user-held
256	or local-only result must be labeled accordingly. If blocked partway, preserve the
257	actual operation/commit state and leave the actionable handoff above; a sync failure
258	after token closure does not require a replacement token. Do not start over blindly.
259	
260	## Exceptions with their own transaction
261	
262	**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. A verified repair, a pending table verification and a quarantine are distinct outcomes. Quarantine may close triage without making evidence citable. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for selectors, mode overrides and the explicit terminal-failure policy.
263	
264	- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
265	  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
266	  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
267	  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
268	- Fresh `wiki-init` can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
269	  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
270	  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
271	- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
272	  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
273	  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.
274	
275	## Executable lifecycle templates
276	
277	Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
278	comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the
279	close step after a failed edit/check. These examples assume a configured upstream
280	and no explicit user hold, so they include the push step. For an explicit local-only
281	request, omit that step and report the unpushed commit. The close is scoped with
282	`--paths-file`; to close and publish in one command, replace the `op-commit` and
283	`wiki-sync` lines with `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --title 'Task title'` (add
284	`--paths-file <ledger>` to scope it explicitly).
285	
286	```powershell
287	$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
288	try {
289	  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
290	  $wikiOpToken = node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink
291	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not open wiki operation' }
292	  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
293	  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since $wikiOpToken <path>...
294	  'Validated task narrative' | node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken
295	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not log wiki operation' }
296	  $wikiLedger = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "wiki-ledger-$wikiOpToken.json"
297	  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since $wikiOpToken --out $wikiLedger
298	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not build the wiki operation ledger' }
299	  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
300	  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken --paths-file $wikiLedger
301	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not commit wiki operation' }
302	  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs'
303	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki update is committed locally but not verified published' }
304	} finally {
305	  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
306	}
307	```

312	  wiki_op_token=$(node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink) || exit

# Completion for vault mutations

Use this contract for every ordinary vault write, including standalone clipping,
authoring and applying triage decisions. Read-only search, query, health, freshness
and preview work do not open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes.

`index.md`'s generated catalog is derived: regenerate it with `index-gen.mjs`,
never hand-edit its fence or read-modify-write the file. Manual framing outside
the fence is preserved. A catalog already dirty from another writer remains
theirs: refresh safe project catalogs separately and report a deferred global
refresh rather than adopt foreign edits merely to close this operation.

**Own the update through verified publication.** An authorized wiki edit includes
validation, the scoped operation commit, and pushing to its configured upstream
with `wiki-sync.mjs`, followed by remote verification. Finish those steps without
asking a separate routine permission question. An explicit user instruction to
hold publication or keep the work local overrides this default. A local commit
or a closed token alone does not publish the update. If a remote is absent or sync
fails, report the work as unpublished with its exact next action. Never create a
remote or repository merely to satisfy this rule. A token is not resolved merely
because its file was deleted; account for the work and verify the outcome.

1. **Resolve scope and authorization.** Read the vault's instructions. Existing
   session authorization counts: a request to make a wiki update includes its
   normal commit-and-sync completion unless an explicit hold applies. A request to
   answer/search does not authorize filing a new page. Purge requires its specific
   reviewed plan and publication approval; do not replace those with this rule.
2. **Open before the first write.** Run `op-begin.mjs --op <op>` and save its token.
   On task resumption, reconcile a saved token before opening another one. Keep
   the operation type, title, owned-path ledger, log path and last completed phase
   with it so recovery can distinguish unfinished work from an already closed step.
   It snapshots already-dirty paths; `op-commit` excludes them. It does not isolate
   simultaneous edits to the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets; preserve
   pre-existing changes and report exclusions instead of sweeping them into a commit.
   With concurrent writers, maintain an explicit ledger of the exact vault-relative
   files this operation owns, including its log and generated catalogs when safe.
   Let the writers keep it: give `--since <token>` to every clipper, to `log-entry.mjs`,
   to `index-gen.mjs` and to `refresh-catalogs.mjs --apply`, each of which records the
   exact path it writes (unquoted UTF-8, so a name with an em dash survives), and record
   a page you wrote with your own file tools using `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token>
   <path>...`. `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <file>` writes the JSON array
   `--paths-file` takes and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong: recorded
   paths that were already dirty before `op-begin`, recorded paths that are not dirty
   now, and changed paths nobody recorded (another writer's, or one you forgot; it
   never claims them). Do not rebuild the set from `git show` or `git status`: git
   prints a non-ASCII name in quotes with octal escapes unless told otherwise, and a
   name lost that way is lost without an error.
   Pass a JSON array of those paths using `op-commit.mjs --paths-file <file>`;
   keep the manifest under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. This narrows the
   newly dirty delta and reports other new paths as outside scope. A ledger path that
   was already dirty when you ran `op-begin` is refused, not skipped: `op-commit` exits 1,
   names it and keeps the token. If this operation wrote it, run the same `op-commit`
   again with `--include <path>` for each (or `--include-from <file>`); if another writer
   owns it, take it out of the ledger. **Create new files only after `op-begin`**: a page
   written first counts as already dirty. It does not isolate simultaneous edits to the
   same file.
   **The guard.** `op-commit` without `--paths-file` commits everything that became
   dirty since `op-begin`, which cannot tell this operation's new files from another
   open operation's. So while any other operation token exists, of any age (age cannot
   show that an operation was abandoned), such a close is refused: `op-commit: this
   close has no --paths-file and another operation is open: <token> (<op>), ...`. It
   exits 1, commits nothing, keeps the token, and prints the way out: `op-ledger.mjs
   show --since <token> --out <ledger>`, then the same `op-commit` with `--paths-file
   <ledger>`. There is no override flag. A close with `--paths-file` is unchanged, and
   with no other token open an unscoped close behaves as before. Every refused close
   (this one, a pre-dirty ledger path, an evidence mismatch) appends a counts-only
   line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl`; see "Refusal record" below.
   When the ledger carries a receipt that records its own byte length and SHA-256
   (captured JSON or log evidence), also pass `--evidence-map <file>`: a JSON object
   of ledger path to `{ "bytes": N, "sha256": "<64 lower-case hex>" }`, kept beside
   the ledger. After staging and before committing, `op-commit` compares each staged
   blob with its declaration. On a mismatch it commits nothing, unstages, keeps the
   token, and names the file, the declared and stored size and hash, and the exact
   `.gitattributes` line (`<path> -text`) that keeps the bytes. Add that one line,
   list `.gitattributes` in the ledger and rerun. It never edits an attribute itself,
   and ordinary Markdown keeps the vault's text policy. A pass is reported as its own
   `evidence:` line, separate from the index notice.
   An existing enclosing operation may own delegated clips and triage bookkeeping;
   record who closes it rather than opening a second operation unnecessarily.
3. **Edit and validate.** Check the requested behavior/content, valid frontmatter,
   canonical placement and exact citation/link targets. Preserve raw bodies and
   unrelated changes. `reviewed` advances only for factual verification. On uncertain
   write timeouts inspect the target before retrying; do not make a duplicate page.
4. **Refresh affected catalogs once.** For project authoring run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-catalogs.mjs" --project <slug> --apply` instead of three separate generators. It builds one vault graph, updates only that project's backlog and MOC, then the global index; unchanged files are not rewritten. Leave out `--apply` for a dry run: it writes nothing and its `changed` list is the list an apply would change, and `--diff` prints each changed file's removed and added lines to stderr. With concurrent writers, pass `--paths-file <JSON ownership ledger>` so another writer's uncommitted pages stay out: a page is listed when it is in the last commit or the ledger names it, and a page another writer has only staged is not. A line the catalog already has for such a page, put there by that writer's own run, is kept. Inspect the returned `changed` paths; with `--since <token>`, an `--apply` records them in the operation's ledger (a dry run records nothing). Without a project selector it refreshes all projects. Standalone generators remain available and the project generators accept `--project`. A global scan is still needed for cross-project ambiguous names.
5. **Log once.** Pipe a concise narrative into `log-entry.mjs --op <op> --title
   "<title>"`. It writes one uniquely named `log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md`,
   with date/op/title frontmatter and a grep-friendly heading. Use the existing
   operation vocabulary (ingest, discover, query, lint, relink); authoring uses
   relink. Never append to a shared aggregate log; browse through `log.base`. Pass
   `--since <token>`: the entry's name carries a timestamp known only now, and the
   ledger is how it reaches the close.
6. **Commit and inspect.** Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`,
   read what it lists as unclaimed, then `op-commit.mjs --op <op> --title "<title>"
   --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused
   while any other operation is open (the guard, step 2). Verify its result and the actual changed paths. Never `git add -A`.
   The helper attempts a semantic index refresh after committing; inspect notices
   for missing backends, skipped work or partial builds. A commit does not establish
   index freshness. Report a non-git vault as local-only; do not claim a commit.
7. **Push and verify your update.** `op-commit` itself never pushes. The plugin
   scripts own the vault's git, so sync with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"`,
   not a bare `git push`: it fetches, rebases onto the upstream (never a merge commit),
   pushes, retries once when another machine pushed first, and verifies against a fresh
   fetch. Run it after `op-commit`, never between edits; it names any operation still
   open. A conflict aborts the rebase, exits 1 and names the files; the local commits are
   intact. Report it and stop: do not force, resolve by guessing, or claim success.
   `rebase-failed` is different: the rebase never started (usually a held `.git/index.lock`),
   so no files are named and nothing changed. Wait for the other git process, never delete
   a lock, and run `wiki-sync` again. The line gives the lock's age; git records no holder,
   so a lock that stays old with no git process running is for the owner to judge.
   Older versions printed a held lock as a conflict in "unknown files": an empty file list

## Recovery and token ownership

- **Retry the same operation.** After a recoverable failure, inspect the token,
  exact owned files and actual commits before retrying the failed step. Resolve
  an understood cause within the authorized scope without another confirmation.
  A failed Git close keeps its token; retry that `op-commit`, not the edits or an
  already-written log. Never delete a Git lock or guess at a content conflict.
- **Reconcile uncertain completion.** A timeout may have occurred after a commit
  or token removal. Verify the actual commit's subject and path membership, owned
  content and validation state. A completed no-op or already-committed operation
  with a retained token still closes through its own scoped `op-commit`; an empty
  delta alone does not prove completion. If the token is already gone, verify
  closure and continue from the next unfinished step rather than opening a new
  token or replaying work. After a sync rebase, locate the operation through its
  unique log path and recheck the resulting commit instead of relying on its old SHA.
- **Respect holds and ownership.** Do not close a user-held operation. A delegated
  worker reports its owned paths and validation to its enclosing operation's named
  owner rather than closing the parent's token. The hand-off is the ledger: the brief
  gives the worker the parent's token; the worker records each path it writes with
  `op-ledger.mjs add --since <parent token> <path>...` (a clipper it runs takes
  `--since` too) and reports its validation; it never runs `op-commit` or `op-abort`.
  The owner runs `op-ledger.mjs show --since <parent token>`, resolves whatever it
  lists as unclaimed, and closes once. That owner remains responsible for
  the scoped commit, push and remote verification; delegation does not drop the
  publication step. Leave other agents' tokens alone unless ownership was explicitly transferred;
  tokens contain an opening dirty-path snapshot, not proof of who owns later edits.
- **Leave actionable blockers.** If safe progress requires an unresolved conflict,
  missing authorization or another owner's action, retain the operation and record
  its token, owned paths, completed steps, pending work and exact next action. Report
  that blocker or ownership handoff; do not claim completion or silently abandon it.

**Abandoned tokens.** List retained tokens with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-cleanup.mjs"` (a dry run). Older than 24
hours means a review candidate, not proven abandonment; these tokens still block
`wiki-sync --commit-local`. For a verified-abandoned operation you own, with no
unfinished work or user hold, apply cleanup with its explicit `--apply --token <id>`
without another approval. Prefer normal `op-commit` closure when the saved operation
can be completed. `--hours <n>` changes the age filter, with a one-hour minimum;
respect that eligibility and verify removal. Never sweep tokens by age or delete
them manually. Token files are local Git-ignored state, not cross-machine locks.
The paths an operation's writers recorded sit in `<token>.paths.jsonl` beside the
token. `op-commit` (when the close lands), `op-abort` and a stale token removed by
`op-cleanup` take it with them; `op-cleanup` also lists a ledger whose token is
already gone and removes it only with `--apply --token <that id>`.

**Stopping early.** A session that opened an operation and will not finish it, or whose work landed another way, drops its own token with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-abort.mjs" --since <token>`. It removes that one token whatever its age and nothing else: the files the operation wrote stay in the working tree, uncommitted, for a later operation to commit. Do not use it on a token another session holds. Open operations are visible without running a sync: `health` and `session-brief` print a line when any are open, and `wiki-sync` mentions other writers' operations once for a given set of tokens, again when the set changes, and once a day while it stays true.

**Refused sync.** `wiki-sync` refuses to integrate while uncommitted edits overlap files
that the upstream changed: it prints `uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes in
<files>` and exits 3, the one exit code for this refusal (every other failure exits 1).
It changes nothing: no commit, stash or checkout, and the files and open tokens are
untouched. With no operation open the dirty files are hand edits, and the message is that
one line ending `commit them (or finish the operation) and sync again`. With an operation
open the message is longer: one line per overlapping file, `<file>: recorded by operation
<token> (<op>)` when an open operation's recorded ledger names the file and it is still
dirty, otherwise `<file>: not recorded by any open operation`; then `Open operations:
<token> (<op>), ...`; then `If you wrote these edits, finish your operation
(wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>) and sync again.` (the token is filled in only when exactly one
open operation recorded an overlapping file, otherwise the line shows the literal
`<token>`); then `If you did not, leave them exactly as they are:
do not reset, checkout, stash or delete them. Wait for their owner to close the operation, then sync again.` That
last instruction is the rule: a file you did not write is not yours to reset, check out,
stash or delete to get the sync through. Wait, and sync again after its owner closes. The
`recorded by` line is a hint, not proof of ownership. It reads only what writers recorded
with `--since` or `op-ledger.mjs add` (a generated file such as `index.md` is recorded only
when `index-gen` ran with `--since`) and ignores a ledger path that is not dirty now, an
unreadable ledger and the opening snapshot in a token, which says what was already dirty,
not who wrote it. `not recorded by any open operation` therefore does not mean no one is
writing the file. Each refusal also appends a counts-only line to the refusal record below.

**Refusal record.** Each `op-commit` close that is refused and keeps its token, and each
`wiki-sync` that stops on an overlap (see "Refused sync"), appends
one JSON line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl` (local, Git-ignored): `at` (ISO
time), `op`, `kind` and `paths`. `paths` is a number and never a path name. `kind` is
`pre-dirty` (a ledger path already dirty before `op-begin` and not adopted; `paths` is
how many), `evidence` (a declared size or hash that does not match what git would store;
`paths` is the size of the evidence map), `unscoped` (the guard; `paths` is how many
delta paths the close would have committed) or `sync-overlap` (`op` is `wiki-sync`;
`paths` is how many files overlap). A close that lands appends nothing, and a
failed append (a directory in the file's place, a read-only disk) changes neither the
message nor the exit code. `health` prints `Recorded refusals: N (pre-dirty a,
evidence b, unscoped c, sync-overlap d).` only when N is above zero, and `health --json`
always carries `opRefusals` as `{ total, preDirty, evidence, unscoped, syncOverlap }`. The
line was `Recorded op-commit refusals: N (...)` in 0.85.0. Like the open-operations line it
sits outside the defect count. The file is never trimmed by the plugin and a line that is
not a record of a known kind counts as nothing.

commits what one operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. A new
vault's `vault-schema.md` (written by `wiki-init`) carries the same statement; an existing
vault keeps its own file. The Obsidian Git plugin stays installed for its source-control
view and for pulling. Its auto-commit and auto-push must be off (auto commit-and-sync
interval 0, commit on file change off, auto push interval 0): they commit half-finished
operation edits under "vault backup" and leave `op-commit` an empty delta. `wiki-sync`
warns when they are on. Every machine sharing the vault needs the same setting. An
instruction elsewhere that says Obsidian Git is the sync engine is stale.

operation log are recorded, the operation commit is verified (or its precise
limitation reported), and its push and remote publication are verified. A user-held
or local-only result must be labeled accordingly. If blocked partway, preserve the
actual operation/commit state and leave the actionable handoff above; a sync failure
after token closure does not require a replacement token. Do not start over blindly.

**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. A verified repair, a pending table verification and a quarantine are distinct outcomes. Quarantine may close triage without making evidence citable. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for selectors, mode overrides and the explicit terminal-failure policy.

- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
- Fresh `wiki-init` can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.

## Executable lifecycle templates

Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the
close step after a failed edit/check. These examples assume a configured upstream
and no explicit user hold, so they include the push step. For an explicit local-only
request, omit that step and report the unpushed commit. The close is scoped with

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  $wikiOpToken = node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not open wiki operation' }
  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since $wikiOpToken <path>...
  'Validated task narrative' | node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not log wiki operation' }
  $wikiLedger = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "wiki-ledger-$wikiOpToken.json"
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since $wikiOpToken --out $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not build the wiki operation ledger' }
  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken --paths-file $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not commit wiki operation' }
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki update is committed locally but not verified published' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```
